restrictions: Complete fixed-IV SHA3-256 sponge (rate 1088, capacity 512, suffix 0x06, pad10*1), prefix rounds 0 through 5, all 256 output bits; every message is exactly 128 bytes (one block; lane 16 = 0x8000000000000006).

Generic birthday search over N = NB*2^40 messages, NB = 307,990,341,830,783,024,002,353,940 batches (the smallest batch count whose success bound of proof Section 7 under H1 is at least 0.3905; a fixed rule computed by cert.py, no run informs it), in 256*NB groups of 2^32. Group g has a fresh structured 128-byte prefix P_g (5kyguy's family of 6e715d9a): 768 uniform bits in the free lanes 0-4, 6, 7, 9-11, 13, 14; with C4 = L4 ^ L9 ^ L14 and C1 = L1 ^ L6 ^ L11 ^ 0x8000000000000006, L5 = L15 = C4 ^ rotl(C1, 1), L8 = 0, L12 = ~rotl(C4, 1) ^ L2 ^ L7. Message m(g, z) is P_g with LE32(z) XORed into bytes 32..35 and 112..115 (lanes 4 and 14), so round 1 is linear in z (linear structures of Guo, Liu and Song, ASIACRYPT 2016; on this track Th0rgal's 4867f093).

Groups are processed in batches of 256 (one group per bit position of every 256-bit word, bitsliced), z = zperm(gray(t)), t < 2^32 (zperm: a fixed bit permutation, Lemma 12), slots offered in the fixed order decode_slot(q) = 16*(q mod 16) + floor(q/16), q = 0..255. The messages with processing indices q = 2k and q = 2k+1 of batch beta at step t share the pair id n = beta*2^39 + t*2^7 + k.

Each batch (2^32 z-steps x 256 messages) is an exact counted, fully unrolled word-RAM program whose EXACT operation count T = 115,833,416,048,165 (T / 2^32 = 26,969.569 per z-step) is charged: all 8,211 straight-line bodies (one per leaf j = ctz(t) and low-bit view state; leaf j < K = 12 runs in 2^(K-j) states, 2^(31-K) times each; leaf j >= K 2^(31-j) times) are compiled and counted, plus the block-unrolled control: the low bodies of each block pattern form one straight-line chain with no control between them; a high step runs s = s + 1 and 2(j - K + 1) bit-test operations, its body and one jump; one jump ends each chain; 1 + 2(32 - K) operations end the batch. Bodies: t = 0 31,497, low leaves 26,391..30,963, high leaves 727,814..909,938 ops. Batch setup (prefixes, A2, O2P, maintained view words) is a counted 6,237,798-op program, charged as 2^23 per batch; run setup (z/slot tables) 2^19.

bs7's step program (AND-free incremental round 2, lane-complement rounds 3-5 with theta at the store and start planes (10, 61, 34), the round 4-5 cones, the last round on 35 planes, the rotating-frame zero-row transpose, the 5/6-op tagged-id table step) is unchanged except: A2 and O2P are kept at the base point of the low K = 12 Gray bits and 4,095 materialised views hold the maintained O2P words that differ (a fixed XOR of base A2 words; 902,780 words, Lemma 14' (v)), so steps with ctz(t) < K do no round-2 work and steps with ctz(t) >= K patch the base and every maintained view word (Lemma 13); within each 2^K-step block a raw round-3 chi output is reloaded when its inputs' view expressions repeat an earlier position's (Lemma 14), complemented when they differ only by input X's all-ones term, or computed as input X XOR a stored nonlinear chi term when inputs X+1, X+2 repeat (memo2, Lemma 14'); z is enumerated in a fixed permuted Gray order (Lemma 12; bs11's, extended to 12 low bits).

The counted program (generator, compiler, counted simulator, setup generator, certificate) and a self-test that regenerates all 8,211 bodies, prints the exact batch count T = 115,833,416,048,165, checks the control layout and runs every body on the counted simulator against verifier/keccak.py (2,102,016 keys; maintained A2, O2P and view words against a rebuild; 3 x 40 consecutive steps, one from a block start without memo prefill; four replayed z-steps of genuine candidates, two of them checking that every candidate stops at the slot's last writer; the halting path at its three positions; setup) are shipped as proof Appendix A (nine files with SHA-256 markers and an extraction command, including the deterministic generator of the Gray order; package rules admit no other source files). The experiment script and manifest are bs7's, byte-identical; every participant run of the script is listed in proof Section 10.3, and the run list is frozen at 2026-10-09T02:32Z.

Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with 64 registers as our stated assumption (the program uses all 64: at most 62 per compiled body, register-allocated by interval colouring after SSA and store-to-load forwarding, plus the block counter s and the table word c). One six-round permutation costs 1 unit; every executed load, store (direct or register-addressed), logic operation, shift or rotation, add, comparison, conditional branch, immediate move and random word costs 1/1626; constant addresses and immediates are instruction fields. The 64-register reading does not cover a register bank of thousands of words; no bound is claimed under such a reading or a memory-to-memory reading. Stricter readings (one address addition per direct access and one move per ALU immediate, also each shift or rotation amount) are priced in proof Section 9.

Table: S has 2^140 words at address 0, never initialised; the key K < 2^140 is the address; the slot holds TAG*2^128 + n, n the pair id of the last message with key K (TAG uniform, drawn once per run). Hot path: load, XOR with c = TAG*2^128 + n, compare < 2^128, branch, store c, c += 1 after odd q only. A slot whose high half is TAG is a candidate: the branch site's own copy (5kyguy's convention) rebuilds and evaluates the current message, then, last writer first (Lemma 15), member 1 of the stored pair (unless the stored pair is the current one, odd q), stopping if its digest has the current key, else member 0: 2 or 3 units. It halts only on equal digests of distinct messages, else adds the units to CNT and continues (61..108 extra ops by count incl. the jump back, halting <= 92; charged 55 per unit incl. 10 per evaluation), aborting when CNT reaches UCAP = floor(5N^2/2^142) + floor(5N^2/2^149) + 2^93 + 2^63 units. Garbage candidates have expectation <= N*2^-128 for any initial memory.

Time bound in every run (no restarts): T_run <= NB*(T + 2^23)/1626 + 2^19/1626 + (UCAP + 2)*(1 + 55/1626) + (3 + 150/1626) + 1 + 2^100 (charges generating the program and all target-specific search and development by anyone; declared as preprocessing_log2 = 100 and counted once, here; proof Section 8) < 2^124.05198 (log2 124.051978) with T = 115,833,416,048,165 the exact count of one batch, proved by an exact integer inequality at five decimals (proof Section 8; cert.py). The success probability 0.39 (model value 0.3905) relies on the declared heuristic H1 for F1, F2 and the genuine-candidate part of the abort probability (< 2^-100), and on no experiment count; garbage candidates add <= 2^-61 by Markov and equal messages from two groups (F3) < 2^-545, both without heuristic. Memory < 2^145.01 bytes including the whole address span. Output correctness and all resource bounds are unconditional.

This is our deae1126 (bs12, 124.05203; review not_evaluable) with text-only fixes (no inference from experiment trials, the organizer's actual public-seed result, H1's unmeasured quantities and their sensitivity stated, preprocessing declared); bs12 revised our 982bf613 (bs11, 124.07261), which revised df0136bc (bs9, 124.096) and 7e40f784 (bs7, 124.263).

No cryptanalytic weakness of SHA3 is claimed: this is a constant-factor improvement of a full-digest birthday search under the operation-level cost model. Memory is about 2^145 bytes (reported only, not a Pareto improvement).

heuristics.statement: (a) For the failure events F1, F2 and the genuine-candidate part of F4 (proof Section 7), the N = NB*2^40 digests (NB = 307,990,341,830,783,024,002,353,940 batches, Section 7) of the grouped message set {m(g, z)} (independent prefixes P_g, each uniform over the 2^768 structured 128-byte prefixes of Section 2, all z in {0,1}^32, processed in any fixed order chosen independently of the digests, in particular the order of Section 2: batch by batch, t = 0..2^32-1 with z = zperm(gray(t)), slots p = decode_slot(q) = 16*(q mod 16) + floor(q/16) for q = 0..255) behave like N independent uniform 256-bit values, i.e. Pr[F1] <= exp(-N(N-1)/2^257), Pr[F2] <= N^3/6 * 2^-396 and, since the 140-bit key is a fixed function of 140 digest bits, the number Y1 of message pairs with equal keys has E[Y1] <= N^2/2^141 and Var[Y1] <= E[Y1], and, in the same way, the number Y1' of those pairs whose earlier message has an even processing index q and whose later message is not its pair partner (a sub-count chosen without reading a digest) has Var[Y1'] <= E[Y1'] (the relation E[Y1'] <= E[Y1]/2 holds without H1, proof Section 7, so E[Y1'] <= N^2/2^142). (b) Run-selection premise of the evidence: the organizer-executed configuration that the package controls (four layouts, 18-bit masks, N_t = 2^9, 256 trials per experiment) is unchanged from our public packages 949c283b and 5e73af65, and the experiment script and manifest are byte-identical to bs7's (7e40f784); per-trial seeds are derived by the organizer's runner, not by us; the message family is fixed externally (5kyguy, 6e715d9a; their organizer trials of it were not used to choose anything here); the only parameters chosen for this package (storage polarity pi, start planes 10, 61, 34, prefix seed label s3r6-ls128-v1, and, new since bs7, the view count K (10 in bs9 and bs11, 12 here), the Gray order ORDER, the output of the shipped generator ordergen.py (seed 12, extended to 12 low bits), the memo2 rules and threshold, the batch count NB, fixed by the success-bound rule of cert.py, and the units cap UCAP) were set by cost objectives or fixed rules, before or without any of our trials, never from a digest or masked-collision statistic; and our own runs of the experiment script were specified and hashed before our first trial of this family and are all reported in proof Section 10.3, together with every later run by us or by agents working for us up to the run-list freeze of this revision (reviewer runs and exact replays included), none selected, repeated or dropped according to its outcome.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability (Section 7) uses H1, through Pr[F1], Pr[F2] and Pr[2 Y1 + Y1' >= UCAP - 3*2^61] < 2^-100 (Chebyshev; E[Y1'] <= E[Y1]/2 holds without H1 by a symmetry of the slot order, proof Section 7); part (b) concerns only how the experimental support for (a) was obtained. No experiment count enters the success bound: the organizer's counts are witness frequencies only (proof Section 10.3). The garbage-candidate part of the abort (<= 2^-61, Markov on E[Y2] <= N*2^-128 with a uniform run TAG), F3 (< 2^-545, counting), evaluator exactness, verification of every output, and all time, memory and preprocessing bounds are unconditional (the candidate cap makes the time bound hold in every run; the operation count is reproducible from proof Appendix A). For every z, P -> m(P, z) permutes the structured-prefix set (XORing z into the free lanes 4 and 14 keeps C4, C1 and the dependent lanes), so m(g, z) is uniform over that set for every z; cross-group pairs (all but a 2^-96 fraction of pairs) therefore provably collide with probability >= 2^-256 each (Cauchy-Schwarz), and the expected number of colliding pairs is at least (1-2^-96) N(N-1)/2^257 without H1; H1 is needed for the second-moment behaviour behind Pr[F1], for F2 and for Y1 and Y1' (under H1's model the equal-key indicators of distinct pairs are pairwise independent, so Var[Y1'] <= E[Y1'] exactly as for Y1; Y1' is a digest-independent sub-count of Y1's pairs). Bitslicing, batching, the incremental round 2, the materialised Gray views, the round-3 block memo and memo2, the block-unrolled control, the last-writer-first candidate order, the Gray order (a bijection of the 2^32 z values of each batch), the start planes, the dependency cone, the compiler, the 140-bit key, the fixed encodings, the 16-row transpose layout and the pair ids change neither the message set nor any digest value; they fix only the processing order, which depends on (batch, t, q) and never on digests.
heuristics.extrapolation: Tested at scale only, as witness frequencies: four organizer-executed scaled analogues with N_t = 2^9 messages and an 18-bit mask of kept digest bits (N_t^2/2^18 = 1, close to N^2/2^256 = 0.990), all on structured 128-byte prefixes, with digests from an evaluator that shares bs7's counted program geometry (linear-structure incremental round 2 with the program's read-only flips, storage polarity and fixed patch expressions; lane-complement rounds with theta at the store and start planes 10, 61, 34; rounds 4-5 computed in full, then every word outside the Lemma 10 cone replaced by an unrelated constant; last round on the 35 kept planes at the program's key rows; the rotating-frame zero-row transpose in the 16-row layout, checked against the full transpose; the processing order; every key also through the tagged-id table with pair ids and adversarial garbage): 256 groups x 2, 16 x 32, a single group of 512, and 4 x 128 with the varying z bits at 25..31 (bs4's layouts and masks). The script and manifest are bs7's, byte-identical: this package changes only how a batch is evaluated, the candidate order and the batch count, none of which changes a key or the definition of a message (proof Section 10.2). The script's self-checks (the whole 140-bit key of each trial's first 4 messages and of one message at every step t = 2^i against an independent direct sponge, the 22-word supports, the maintained A2 and round-3 input against a rebuild) abort a run on failure. The organizer's public-seed run of these files (deae1126's dossier run 37872901902, target configuration f74fe7d4, report dca34a1f) completed with 106 / 99 / 113 / 112 of 256 (full-width / spread / single-group / high-z), each request twice with identical output. Reading of these counts under this heuristic (not a test, no rejection rule): H1's model at this scale gives a trial success probability 0.393074, i.e. 100.6 expected per request. The counts are witness frequencies only, as the runner allows (its frequency is not an iid success-probability estimate); no interval, p-value, pooled statistic or significance test is drawn from them or from participant runs, and the success bound does not use them. The manifest's 'within sampling error' and the spread scope's 'trials stay independent' are bs7's frozen wording, not asserted here beyond data-flow separation (proof Section 10.2). bs12 predicted 91 / 99 / 105 / 105 (report d160f2ea, our replay R1); R1 ran under the earlier fingerprint 8bc09b76, and the runner's per-trial seeds hash the fingerprint, which the organizer's SHA-256 r37/r38 reorg (commit aff92df) changed to f74fe7d4 (runner.py; the report's target_config_sha256); an unshipped check of ours, consistent with this, finds all 430 returned pairs built from f74fe7d4 seeds and none from 8bc09b76 seeds (proof Section 10.3). We predict no organizer output. Participant runs (untrusted; R1-R4, R5 with 12,288 local trials per layout, C2, V1-V3, Q, and exact replays) are listed with counts and hashes in proof Section 10.3 only to complete the run record; none since bs10's freeze. The claim extrapolates uniform-model behaviour to N = NB*2^40, the 256-bit digest and its 140-bit truncation; F1 and Y1 at full width, F2, Y1' and the F4 margin are not observed at any tested scale.
heuristics.limitations: H1 is not proved. Within a group, round 1 is linear in z and A2 = A2(0) XOR sum_j z_j E_j with fixed group-independent vectors E_j (all-ones on 22 words; Lemmas 1-3), a stronger structure than in a generic search; five further nonlinear chi layers (rounds 2-6) follow, but masked low-width experiments cannot exclude a structural effect that appears only at full width. Within a group the digest has degree at most 2^5 = 32 in z; z has 32 bits, so no degree-based zero-sum exists on any affine subspace of z. Covered only by H1's independence model and not measured by any experiment: F1 and Y1 at full width, F2, Y1', and the 2^-7 (0.78%) margin of the F4 cap; the experiments give witness frequencies of 18-bit masked collisions among 2^9 messages, not estimates. Sensitivity (proof Section 7): by Cauchy-Schwarz non-uniformity of the key's marginal distribution can only raise the cross-group part of E[Y1]; a variance of 2 Y1 + Y1' up to about 2^89 times its bound under H1 keeps the Chebyshev bound on Pr[F4] below the 0.0005 allowance; a relative excess e of its mean up to just below 0.78% keeps F4 negligible; above that the cap binds before the run ends and, as a heuristic approximation, the success probability falls to about 1 - exp(-(N^2/2^257)(1 + 2^-7)/(1 + e)) - Pr[F2]: 0.39 at about e = 0.95%, 0.387 at 2%, 0.378 at 5%, 0.365 at 10%, 0.221 at 100% (0.174 if the excess sits within batches; the time bound holds in every case). The 0.0005 allowance between the model value 0.3905 and the claimed 0.39 is a margin under H1 that no experiment certifies; on its own it absorbs Pr[F2] up to 13 times its bound. Within-group pairs would need an average key-collision probability above about 2^-51, or above about 2^-19 for the pairs of one z-difference, to matter. Part (b) rests partly on checkable facts (the unchanged organizer configuration, the byte-identical script and manifest, the runner's seed derivation, the externally fixed family, cost-only parameter choices reproducible from proof Appendix A) and partly on our statement about our own runs, whose timing cannot be checked; two earlier statements were wrong and are corrected in proof Section 10.3 (df0136bc's run list missed one exact replay made after its freeze; bs12 predicted that the organizer's public-seed run would reproduce our R1, which the reorg's new fingerprint ruled out). Organizer seeds are public; a holdout-nonce rerun by the organizer (supported without any change to the script) is the independent check.
